key_findings: 81 mm of LOS displacement in 35 days — the hanging glacier IS moving
This acceleration period overlaps with the Aug 24 ice break-offs
GOFF pixel offsets failed on this site (45-50° slopes, cm-scale motion)
GUNW InSAR successfully detects the motion despite low coherence (0.10)
Only 3 dates available — insufficient for robust z-score anomaly detection
With more epochs, the GLEWS pipeline WOULD flag this as anomalous

goff_result.reason: GOFF pixel offsets produce noise (85 m artifacts) on 45-50° slopes. The real displacement (~81 mm) is far below GOFF measurement precision (~1-3 m). GOFF is unsuitable for steep hanging glaciers with sub-meter motion.

validation_verdict: PARTIAL SUCCESS — InSAR detects real motion at Weisshorn, confirming the site is unstable. The acceleration toward the Aug 24 break-off is visible. Full anomaly detection requires ≥5 epochs for a robust baseline, which NISAR will accumulate over the coming weeks.
